sentences.text: One more law lives beside the rules, and it explains why the tugs and ships are always talking on channel thirteen.
It’s the Vessel Bridge-to-Bridge Radiotelephone Act.
It requires certain vessels on American waters to keep a listening watch on the bridge-to-bridge channel, so that captains can speak to each other directly.
Power-driven vessels of twenty meters or more.
Vessels of one hundred gross tons or more carrying one or more passengers for hire.
Towing vessels of twenty-six feet or more, and dredges and floating plant working in or near a channel.
The watch is kept on VHF channel thirteen in most areas, and the person keeping it must be able to communicate in English.
So is your six-pack boat required to take part?
Any time you’re near a ship channel, keep one radio on thirteen and one on sixteen.
When a tug captain says, I’ll see you on one whistle, you’ll know he means port to port, and you’ll know he’s talking to you.
